q: 301. A traverse deflection angle is .............
options: the difference between the included angle and 180°
the difference between 360° and the included angle
explain: A deflection angle is the angle which a survey line makes with the prolongation of the preceding line. It is calculated by subtracting the included angle from 180°.

q: 302. The size of plane table is .............
explain: While various sizes exist, the standard size for a large plane table used in professional surveying is typically 600 mm x 750 mm.

q: 303. When the whole circle bearing of a traverse line is between 90° and 180° then .............
options: the latitude is positive and departure is negative
the departure is positive and latitude is negative
both the latitude and departure are positive
both the latitude and departure are negative
explain: The range 90° to 180° falls in the second quadrant (S-E). In this quadrant, Latitude (L cos θ) is South (negative) and Departure (L sin θ) is East (positive).

q: 304. The latitude and departure of a traverse line are both positive when the whole circle bearing of the line lies in the .............
explain: In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), both sine and cosine values are positive, resulting in positive Latitude (North) and positive Departure (East).

q: 305. When the latitudes and departures are so adjusted that the algebraic sum of the latitudes and departures are equal to zero, the operation is called .............
explain: Balancing the traverse is the process of adjusting observed latitudes and departures to eliminate the closing error so that the traverse forms a mathematically closed figure.

q: 306. When the angular and linear measurements are equally precise in traversing, the balancing of a traverse is done by .............
explain: Bowditch's rule (Compass Rule) is used when linear and angular measurements are of equal precision. It assumes errors in linear measurements are proportional to √L.

q: 307. The principle of working from whole to part is used in surveying because .............
options: survey work can be completed quickly
explain: By establishing a primary control network first (the whole) and then filling in details (the part), local errors are contained and do not accumulate across the entire project.

q: 308. During chaining along a straight line, the leader of the party has 4 arrows in his hand while the follower has 6. Distance of the follower from the starting point is .............
explain: The number of arrows held by the follower indicates the number of full chain lengths completed from the starting point.

q: 309. A metallic tape is made of .............
explain: Metallic tapes are made of waterproof linen reinforced with fine brass or copper wires to prevent stretching.

q: 310. An angle made by a survey line with the prolongation of the proceeding line, is known as .............
explain: A deflection angle is the angle between the preceding line's extension and the next line in the traverse.

q: 311. A deflection angle in a traverse is equal to the .............
options: difference between the included angle and 180°
difference between 360° and the included angle and 180°
sum of the included angel and 180°
explain: In any traverse, the deflection angle at a station is 180° minus the internal included angle (or included angle - 180° for external).

q: 312. Pantagraph is used for .............
explain: A pantagraph is a mechanical linkage based on parallelograms used to copy a plan at a different scale (reduction or enlargement).

q: 313. In chain surveying, perpendiculars to the chain line, are set out by .............
explain: Optical squares and cross-staffs are the primary instruments used in chain surveying to set out perpendicular offsets (90° angles).

q: 314. Profile leveling is usually done for determining .............
explain: Profile leveling (longitudinal leveling) is performed to find the elevations of points at known distances along a fixed line, such as a road or railway centerline.

q: 315. The 'point of curve' of a simple circular curve is .............
explain: The point of curve (PC) is the point where the straight alignment (tangent) ends and the circular curve begins; it is the point of commencement.

q: 316. Ramsden eye-piece consists of .............
options: two convex lenses short distance apart
two concave lenses short distance apart
one convex lens and one concave lens short distance apart
two plano-convex lenses short distance apart, with the convex surfaces facing each other
explain: A Ramsden eyepiece consists of two identical plano-convex lenses with their curved surfaces facing each other, placed at a distance equal to 2/3 the focal length of one lens.

q: 317. Designation of a curve is made by .............
options: angle subtended by a chord of any length
angle subtended by an arc of specified length
explain: In engineering practice, a curve is primarily designated either by its Radius (R) or by its Degree of Curvature (D).

q: 318. For the locating a distant object visible from two transit stations, the method usually preferred to is .............
options: angles and distance from transit stations
angle from one transit station and distance from the other
explain: When an object is distant or inaccessible, the method of intersection (measuring angles from two known stations) is the most efficient and accurate.

q: 319. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is .............
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinate of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Independent coordinates (Total Coordinates) are most reliable because errors in plotting one station do not affect the plotting of subsequent stations.

q: 320. The orthographical projection of a traverse leg upon the reference meridian is known, as .............
explain: The projection of a line on the North-South meridian is called the Latitude; the projection on the East-West line is the Departure.

q: 321. The co-ordinate of a point measured perpendicular to the parallel, is called .............
explain: Total latitude is the coordinate of a point measured relative to a reference parallel (usually the Equator or a custom East-West axis).

q: 322. Total latitude of a point is positive if it lies .............
explain: By convention in surveying, Northings (Latitude North) are considered positive and Southings are negative.

q: 323. The altitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by .............
explain: Latitude (often referred to here as altitude in context of projection) = L cos θ, where L is the length and θ is the reduced bearing.

q: 324. In a closed traverse, sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of east departures exceeds the sum of west departures then, the closing line will lie in .............
explain: If ΣS > ΣN, the error in Latitude is South, so the correction is North. If ΣE > ΣW, the error in Departure is East, so the correction is West. Thus the closing line (the correction) lies in the North-West quadrant.

q: 325. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known .............
explain: This describes the fundamental definition of balancing a traverse to ensure closure.

q: 326. If the angular measurements of a traverse are more precise than its linear measurements, balancing of the traverse, is done by .............
explain: The Transit Rule is applied when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements (often used for theodolite traverses).

q: 327. The branch of surveying in which both horizontal and vertical positions of a point, are determined by making in instrumental observations, is known .............
explain: Tacheometry is a branch of angular surveying in which horizontal and vertical distances are determined by optical observations on a staff, eliminating chaining.

q: 328. The method generally preferred to for contouring an undulating area, is .............
explain: Tacheometry is ideal for undulating or hilly terrain because it allows for rapid elevation and distance measurement without needing to physically measure over rough ground.

q: 329. A line joining some fixed points on the main survey lines, is called a .............
explain: A tie line joins fixed points on main lines to enable the location of interior details and to check the accuracy of the framework.

q: 330. A base line in a chain survey .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the survey or locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixes up the directions of all other lines
explain: The base line is the longest and most important line in a chain survey, providing the backbone for the entire framework and detail location.

q: 331. A plumb bob is required .............
options: when measuring distances along slopes in a hilly country
for accurate centering of a theodolite over a station mark
for testing the vertically of ranging poles
explain: A plumb bob is an essential tool for transferring points vertically, centering instruments, and ensuring verticality.

q: 332. Chain surveying is most suitable when .............
options: area to be surveyed is small
ground is fairly level and open with simple details
plans are required on a large scale
explain: Chain surveying is limited by its simplicity; it is best for small, flat, uncomplicated areas where high-precision angular work isn't required.

q: 333. The degree of the curve is the angle subtended by a chord of ............. length.
explain: In India and many other regions, the standard chord length used to define the Degree of Curve (D) is 30 meters (or sometimes 20m, but 30m is the standard in most classic textbooks).

q: 334. If L is the specified length of a tape, L1 its actual length and S the measured distance, then the true distance is given by the formula .............
explain: True Distance = (Actual Length / Nominal Length) x Measured Distance. If the tape is longer than specified, the recorded distance is too short, and vice versa.

q: 335. Metric chains are generally available in .............
explain: Standard IS metric chains are manufactured in lengths of 5, 10, 20, and 30 meters. 20m and 30m are the most common in field work.

q: 336. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction is .............
explain: Reciprocal leveling involves taking sights from both ends of a line (e.g., across a river) to cancel out errors from earth curvature, atmospheric refraction, and instrument adjustment.

q: 337. While measuring with a metallic tape of 30 m length pull should be applied .............
explain: A standard pull of about 3 kg (or 30 Newtons) is usually recommended for metallic tapes to counteract sag and ensure accuracy.

q: 338. The ratio of the distances at which a stated length can be distinguished by the telescope and the human eye, respectively, is called .............
explain: Magnification power is the ratio of the size of the image formed on the retina when seen through a telescope to the size of the image when seen by the naked eye.

q: 339. The first reading from a level station is .............
explain: The first reading taken after setting up a level is always a Back Sight (BS) taken on a point of known elevation.

q: 340. Bergchund is a topographical feature in .............
explain: A Bergschrund is a crevasse that forms where a moving glacier ice mass separates from the stagnant ice or rock above.

q: 341. A check line in a chain surveying .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: The sole purpose of a check line (proof line) is to verify the accuracy of the framework measurements during plotting.

q: 342. A tie line in a chain surveying .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: Tie lines are secondary lines used to pick up interior details that are too far from the main survey lines to be accurately measured by offsets.

q: 343. Then the position of a point is to be located accurately by a perpendicular offset, the direction of perpendicular is set out by means of .............
explain: An optical square is a small, portable instrument used for setting out right angles to a line with higher precision than a cross-staff.

q: 344. The accuracy in laying down the perpendicular offsets and in measuring them depends upon .............
explain: Accuracy requirements vary based on how small the scale of the map is, how far the point is from the chain line, and how critical the object is to the survey.

q: 345. The limiting length of the offset is ............. when its perpendicular direction is set out by an eye.
explain: When setting offsets by eye (without an instrument), the maximum length is generally restricted to 15m to keep the error within permissible limits.

q: 346. The instrument used for setting out an offset at a right angle, is called .............
explain: While cross-staffs can do this, the optical square is the specific high-accuracy choice among these options for 90-degree offsets.

q: 347. The adjustable cross-staff is used for setting out an offset .............
explain: An adjustable cross-staff consists of two cylinders that can be rotated relative to each other, allowing any angle to be set and observed.

q: 348. For setting out an offset at an angle 45°, ............. cross-staff is used.
explain: The French cross-staff is octagonal and has sights that allow angles of 45° and 90° to be set out.

q: 349. The relief representation on the map can be depicted .............
explain: Relief (topography) can be shown using contours, spot heights, hachures, hill shading, or tinting/layering.

q: 350. Pick up the odd instrument .............
explain: Prismatic compasses, theodolites, and sextants are primarily used to measure angles. A dumpy level is used specifically for measuring vertical differences in elevation (leveling).

q: 351. For the Abney clinometer the semi-circular arc is graduated as
explain: The Abney clinometer's arc is graduated from 0° at the center to 90° on either side to measure both angles of elevation and depression.

q: 352. To use the Abney clinometer as Abney level the vernier should read
options: it is not possible to use clinometer as hand level
explain: When the vernier is set to 0°, the line of sight becomes horizontal, allowing the clinometer to function as a basic hand level.

q: 353. An instrument resembling an alidade is
explain: A tangent clinometer (or Indian clinometer) consists of two vanes similar to an alidade and is used on a plane table to determine the heights of objects.

q: 354. If D is the degree of the curve of radius R, the exact length of its specified chord, is
options: radius of the curve × sine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × sine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × cosine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × tangent of half the degree
explain: Using trigonometry, the chord length $L = 2R sin(D/2)$. Since $2R$ is the diameter, the expression is diameter $	imes sin(D/2)$.

q: 355. When the length of a chord is less than the peg interval, it is known as
explain: A normal chord equals the peg interval (usually 20m or 30m). Any chord shorter than this, typically found at the beginning or end of a curve, is a sub-chord.

q: 356. A plain scale is used to read
explain: A plain scale represents two units or a unit and its subdivision (e.g., meters and decimeters).

q: 357. A diagonal scale is used to read ............ dimensions.
explain: Diagonal scales are used to represent three consecutive units, such as meters, decimeters, and centimeters.

q: 358. A scale which has a common representative fraction, but read in different measures, is called a
explain: Comparative scales (or corresponding scales) have the same R.F. but graduate in different units, like miles and kilometers.

q: 359. In a direct vernier, the smallest division of a vernier is ............ the smallest division of its primary scale.
explain: In a direct vernier, $(n-1)$ divisions of the main scale are divided into $n$ divisions on the vernier, making each vernier division slightly shorter than a main scale division.

q: 360. Measurements taken with a wrong scale can be corrected by using the relation
options: true length = (correct scale / wrong scale) × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)² × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)³ × measured length
explain: Linear correction is proportional to the ratio of the scales. For area, the ratio would be squared; for volume, cubed.

q: 361. If x is the smallest division on the main scale and n are the number of divisions on the vernier, then the least count of the vernier is
explain: The least count is the difference between the smallest division of the main scale and the vernier scale, which mathematically simplifies to $x/n$.

q: 362. An average length of a pace is
explain: The average length of a human step (pace) is generally considered to be 80 cm (or about 32 inches) for surveying purposes.

q: 363. The method of measuring distance by pacing is chiefly used in
explain: Pacing is a rough method of distance measurement suitable for the rapid, approximate data gathering required in reconnaissance.

q: 364. Deviation of the actual road gradient from the proposed contour gradient uphill side, involves
options: earth work on the centre line
explain: If the road is shifted towards the uphill side of the proposed contour gradient, it necessitates cutting into the hill (excavation).

q: 365. Two hill tops A and B 20 km apart are intervened by a third top C. If the top most contour of the three hill tops are of the same value, state whether the line of sight AB
options: passes below the hill top C
passes below the hill top C
explain: Due to the earth's curvature, the line of sight between two points at the same elevation will pass below the actual ground level of an intervening point of that same elevation.

q: 366. The best method of interpolation of contours, is by
explain: Interpolation by arithmetical calculation (computation) is the most accurate method, though it is slower than estimation or graphical methods.

q: 367. For preparation of contour plan for a route survey
options: method of trace contour is used
method of cross profile is used
indirect method of contouring is used
explain: In route surveys for roads or railways, cross-sections (profiles) are taken at regular intervals along the centerline to determine the topography of the narrow strip.

q: 368. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The standard acceptable error in interpolated elevations from a contour map is generally taken as half of the contour interval.

q: 369. While surveying a plot of land by plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: A major advantage of plane table surveying is that the map is drafted in the field while the surveyor can compare the plot with the actual ground.

q: 370. The distance between steps for measuring downhill to obtain better accuracy
options: decreases with decrease of weight of the chain
explain: In the 'stepping method' of chaining on sloping ground, steps must be shorter as the slope gets steeper to maintain a horizontal chain and minimize errors.

q: 371. If a tacheometer is fitted with an anallatic lens
options: additive constant is 100, multiplying constant is zero
multiplying constant is 100, additive constant is zero
both multiplying and additive constants are 100
both multiplying and additive constants are 50
explain: The anallatic lens is a special convex lens fitted in a tacheometer to make the additive constant (f+c) zero, simplifying distance calculations to D = Ks.

q: 372. In an adjusted level, when the bubble is central, the axis of the bubble tube becomes parallel to
explain: For an instrument to be in perfect adjustment, the axis of the bubble tube must be parallel to the line of collimation so that the line of sight is horizontal when the bubble is centered.

q: 373. Height of instrument method of leveling is
options: more accurate than rise and fall method
less accurate than rise and fall method
quicker and less tedious for large number of intermediate sights
explain: The HI (Height of Collimation) method is faster for projects with many intermediate sights (like longitudinal sections) because it requires fewer calculations than the Rise and Fall method.

q: 374. The shape of vertical curve generally provided is
explain: Parabolic curves are preferred for vertical curves because they provide a constant rate of change of grade, leading to a smoother transition.

q: 375. An instrument used for ranging is
explain: A line ranger is a small optical instrument used to establish intermediate points on a straight line between two distant stations without the need for signals.

q: 376. Survey plotting can be done with an accuracy of
explain: The limit of human vision and the precision of fine drafting pencils generally limits plotting accuracy on paper to approximately 0.25 mm.

q: 377. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: clockwise or anticlockwise from North/South whichever is nearer...
explain: In the Reduced Bearing (RB) or Quadrantal system, bearings are measured from either North or South towards East or West, whichever is closer, ranging from 0° to 90°.

q: 378. In a whole circle bearing system N25°15'W corresponds to
explain: To convert N 25°15' W to WCB: 360° - 25°15' = 334°45' (since the bearing is in the 4th quadrant).

q: 379. If the fore bearing of a line is 36°15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since 36°15' is less than 180°, we add 180°: 36°15' + 180° = 216°15'.

q: 380. If the fore bearing of a line is N26°35'W, its back bearing will be
explain: In the Quadrantal system, the back bearing has the same numerical value but opposite cardinal directions (N becomes S, W becomes E).

q: 381. When the whole circle bearing of two lines AB and AC are 115° and 41° respectively, then the included angle BAC will be
explain: The included angle BAC is the difference between the bearings of the two lines: 115° - 41° = 74°.

q: 382. The horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line is called
explain: Azimuth is the horizontal angle measured clockwise from the true north (true meridian) to the survey line.

q: 383. The horizontal angle between the truth meridian and magnetic meridian is known as
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle by which the magnetic needle deviates from the true north at a specific location.

q: 384. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: The magnetic dip (angle between the needle and horizontal) is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° at the magnetic poles.

q: 385. Usefulness of plane table is enhanced by providing
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer allows the plane table surveyor to determine the heights of points and ground slopes effectively.

q: 386. For the revision of an existing survey with the help of plane table we generally use
explain: Resection is used to establish the current position of the plane table on the map by sighting back to points already plotted.

q: 387. A point determined by resection on a plane table is called
explain: A 'fix' is the location of the plane table instrument station on the drawing sheet determined through the resection process.

q: 388. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distance directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs, allowing the surveyor to compute distances and elevations optically rather than using a tape or chain.

q: 389. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation ensures that the map is correctly aligned with the cardinal directions on the ground, making all lines on the paper parallel to their ground counterparts.

q: 390. In setting up a plane table at any station
options: both leveling and centering are done simultaneously
explain: In modern practice, leveling and centering are performed at the same time to ensure the board is horizontal and the point is accurately represented above the ground station.

q: 391. In tacheometrical observations, vertical staff holding is generally preferred to normal staffing, due to
options: minimum effect of careless holding on the result
explain: Holding the staff vertically is easier for the staff-man and results in smaller errors if the staff is slightly out of plumb compared to trying to hold it normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight.

q: 392. In tangential tacheometry, an ordinary level staff is used
explain: Tangential tacheometry calculations assume the staff is held perfectly vertical so that the tangent values of the observed vertical angles can be applied.

q: 393. Horizontal distances obtained tacheometrically are corrected for
explain: For very long sights, tacheometric readings must be corrected for the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction, which affect the perceived staff intercept.

q: 394. Tilt of the staff in stadia tacheometry increases the intercept if it is
options: away from the telescope pointing down hill
away from the telescope pointing up-hill
explain: When the staff is tilted away from the telescope while pointing up-hill, the intercept (distance between hairs) appears larger than it would be if held truly vertical.

q: 395. The intercept of a staff
options: is maximum if the staff is held truly normal...
is minimum if the staff is held truly normal...
decreases if the staff is tilted away from normal
increases if the staff is tilted towards normal
explain: The staff intercept is at its mathematical minimum when the staff is held exactly normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight.

q: 396. If vertical angles of inclined sights do not exceed 10° and non-verticality of the staff remains within 1° stadia system...
options: staff normal as well as vertical
explain: For small vertical angles (under 10°), holding the staff vertical is the standard practice in stadia tacheometry as it simplifies the reduction of readings to horizontal distances.

q: 397. The vertical distance above or below the datum is called
explain: Both 'Reduced Level' (RL) and 'Elevation' refer to the vertical distance of a point relative to a specific reference datum.

q: 398. A back sight indicates the ............ of the instrument.
explain: A back sight is the first reading taken after the instrument is set up on a new station, taken on a point of known elevation.

q: 399. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic declination is termed as
explain: Isogonic lines (isogons) connect points on the earth's surface where the magnetic declination is the same at a given time.

q: 400. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination is subject to various changes over time, including secular, annual, and diurnal variations.
